sentences.text: This extinct animal was the largest known member of its genus, with an estimated body mass of about 3.9 kg.
Researchers Hanneke J. M. Meijer, Thomas Sutikna, E. Wahyu Saptomo, and Matthew W. Tocheri described this newly identified species, Megapodius rokusi, in 2026.
The study details a new megapode from the Pleistocene of Liang Bua on Flores, Indonesia.
Identified as a type of megapode, this extinct animal lived during the Late Pleistocene.
The species belongs to the genus Megapodius, which is part of the family Megapodiidae and the class Reptilia.
The fossil remains date to the Pleistocene epoch, specifically the Late Pleistocene.
